title: Jim Corbett National Park Travel Guide | Safari, Museum & Garjia Devi Temple,
content:
Jim Corbett National Park,

Jim Corbett National Park, located in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand, is much more than just a forest - it’s a living story of India’s wildlife heritage. Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, it was later renamed after the legendary hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett, who dedicated his life to protecting wildlife and raising awareness about tigers.

Spread across 1,300 square kilometers, the park is home to over 600 species of birds, 50 species of mammals, and 25 species of reptiles, including the Royal Bengal Tiger, Asian elephants, leopards, gharials, and deer. The park is divided into different zones like Dhikala, Bijrani, Jhirna, Dhela, and Durga Devi, each offering a unique landscape and wildlife experience.

But Corbett is not only about safaris. A visit here lets you experience a mix of adventure, history, and spirituality. The Corbett Museum in Kaladhungi, once Jim Corbett’s own home, is filled with his writings, guns, and stories that give you a glimpse into the man behind tiger conservation. Just a short drive away lies the Garjia Devi Temple, perched on a huge rock in the middle of the Kosi River. This temple is not only sacred for locals but also offers a magical view of nature.

Whether you’re here for a thrilling jeep safari, to walk through history at the museum, or to seek blessings at the temple, Jim Corbett gives you an experience that blends wildlife, culture, and peace all in one journey

Best Time to Visit :

  • November to February (Peak Season): Cool weather (5°C - 0°C), best for safaris and tiger spotting.
  • March to June (Moderate Season): Warm (20°C - 35°C), good for safaris and birdwatching.
  • July to September (Low Season): Rainy (25°C - 30°C), most safari zones closed except Jhirna and Dhela.

Ticket & Safari Cost in Jim Corbett

  • Day Safari (Jeep): ₹4,000-₹6,000 per jeep (max 6 persons). Price depends on zone.
  • Canter Safari (Dhikala Zone): ₹1,500-₹2,000 per person. Good for larger groups.
  • Entry Fee (Indians): ₹200-₹500 per person (varies by zone).
  • Entry Fee (Foreigners): ₹900-₹1,500 per person (varies by zone).
  • Corbett Museum Fee: ₹10 (Indian), ₹50 (Foreigner).
  • Garjia Devi Temple: Free entry.

Booking Tip: Safaris are booked online through the official Jim Corbett website, (It’s best to book 30-45 days in advance, especially for Dhikala)

Distance from City Center:

  • Wildlife Safari (Dhikala/Bijrani/Jhirna gates): Around 5–20 km from Ramnagar.
  • Corbett Museum (Kaladhungi): About 30 km from Ramnagar.
  • Garjia Devi Temple: Just 14 km from Ramnagar.

Things to Do in Jim Corbett :

  • Go on a jeep safari or canter safari in Corbett’s different zones.
  • Visit the Corbett Museum to learn about Jim Corbett’s life and conservation work.
  • Offer prayers at Garjia Devi Temple, a spiritual site loved by locals and tourists.
  • Take a nature walk or birdwatching tour near Kosi River.
  • Enjoy a stay in forest lodges inside the park for a raw jungle experience.
  • Try river rafting (seasonal) on the Kosi River.
  • Relax in eco-resorts around Ramnagar with forest views.

Top 5 Places to Visit Near Jim Corbett (within 50 km) :

1- Sitabani Forest Reserve (20 km): Peaceful forest area for bird lovers.

2- Corbett Waterfall (25 km): A hidden gem surrounded by forests.

3- Kaladhungi (30 km): Village with Corbett Museum.

4- Ramnagar (0 km): Main entry point, good for markets and local food.

5- Kosi River (flows near park): Scenic river for walks and rafting.

6- Nainital (65 km, slightly beyond 50): Can be combined in a trip.

excerpt: Jim Corbett National Park is not just about jungle safaris — it’s also about history and spirituality. While the safari gives you a thrilling chance to see tigers and elephants, the Corbett Museum tells the story of India’s first conservation hero, and the Garjia Devi Temple adds a cultural touch to your journey. Together, they make Corbett one of the most diverse travel experiences in Uttarakhand.
